property_summary: For any caller, after c.initialize() the public getter c.owner() must return that caller (the address stored at initialization); the buggy M always returns address(0), violating this for any non-zero deployer.

For any caller and any new owner, after transferring ownership the stored owner() equals the transferred address regardless of who queries it; the mutant instead returns msg.sender, so it returns the querying caller rather than the set owner whenever they differ.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address,address): Ownable: caller is not the owner
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address,address): owner() must return the transferred owner regardless of caller

property_summary: After a single initialize() by any actor, c.owner() must report that stored owner to every caller; the mutant returns msg.sender, so a different querying caller observes a wrong owner.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): owner() must report the stored owner to any caller

property_summary: owner() must return the stored owner set at initialization (or transferred), independent of msg.sender/tx.origin; the mutant returns tx.origin so it diverges whenever the caller is not the stored owner.

For any caller who is not the owner and any nonzero new owner, transferOwnership must revert (so ownership stays with the original owner), but the mutant lets anyone take ownership, changing c.owner() after the call.

Ownership can never become the zero address via transferOwnership: for any fuzzed newOwner the reference contract either reverts or leaves a nonzero owner(), while the mutant accepts address(0) and c.owner() becomes zero.

For any fuzzed candidate, a successful transferOwnership(newOwner) must set owner() exactly to newOwner and that newOwner must be non-zero (transferOwnership to the zero address must revert); the mutant accepts transferOwnership(address(0)), after which owner() no longer matches a valid transferrable owner and the revert guarantee is lost.

For any caller who is owner, calling transferOwnership(nonZero newOwner) must set c.owner() to newOwner and be callable only by the owner; the buggy version never updates the owner, so after a transfer c.owner() remains the old owner instead of the fuzzed newOwner.

For any non-zero address, the owner's call to transferOwnership(newOwner) must succeed (only the zero address is forbidden); the mutant additionally forbids transferring to the current owner, so it reverts when newOwner equals the owner.

For any address, initializing C as that address and calling transferOwnership to the current owner must succeed (a permitted self-transfer leaving ownership unchanged); the mutant forbids transferring to the current owner and reverts, breaking the rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): self-transfer to current owner must be allowed and ownership must persist

property_summary: After initialize and updateAlloSettings, for any nonzero address passed by the owner, updateRoundImplementation stores it and c.roundImplementation() always equals that address; the mutant accepts zero addresses too, so for a zero input P reverts while M stores address(0).

After any successful updateRoundImplementation call, c.roundImplementation() must be nonzero (P reverts on the zero address so it never stores 0); the mutant, having dropped the require, stores address(0) and violates this for a zero-address input.

For every address an owner may submit, updateRoundImplementation must never leave the roundImplementation getter at the zero address: the reference either reverts or stores a nonzero address, while the mutant happily stores address(0) when given it.

For any nonzero address set by an owner via updateRoundImplementation, the stored roundImplementation getter must return exactly that address; the mutant always stores address(0), so it returns 0 instead.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): roundImplementation must equal the set value

property_summary: For any non-zero owner-supplied address, updateRoundImplementation stores that address so c.roundImplementation() equals it; the mutant requires the zero address, so any non-zero update reverts and roundImplementation keeps its old value.

For any caller, updateRoundImplementation only changes roundImplementation when the caller is the contract owner; the buggy inverse modifier lets any non-owner change it and blocks the owner, so asserting the post-call value equals the requested implementation (with actor=owner) distinguishes P from M.
